clue.text: Bird requiring introduction of odd cage, note, one with many sides

indicators.note: the bird needs something introduced into it, so the rearranged letters go inside its name

parts.note: the dodo is the extinct flightless bird

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters of cage are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A birdkeeper needs a strange many-sided cage for their pet.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'one' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay: 'note' gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-sided polygon is a figure with many sides; the Greek roots mean twelve angles.

clue.text: Cylinder filled with first of Ukraine's wheat

indicators.note: the cylinder is filled, so another letter goes inside it

parts.note: a drum is a cylindrical container

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Ukraine's is taken

explanation.surface: A silo full of Ukraine's grain harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is the hard variety of wheat milled for pasta, an example of the cereal.

clue.text: Anything supplied by doctor is a dose of medicine?

indicators.note: the second piece is provided by, and follows, the doctor

parts.note: aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: A patient asks whether everything the doctor hands out counts as a dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anything' is the archaic AUGHT, not the everyday word.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single measured drink of liquid medicine, so a dose; the question mark flags the less common sense.

clue.text: Unfriendly image leading to concern about new chef's special?

indicators.note: the first pieces come before, and lead to, the rest

parts.note: a chill manner is a cold, unfriendly one
an icon is an image or picture

indicators.note: concern goes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: care means concern or worry

explanation.surface: A frosty picture worries a newcomer to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A spicy meat and bean stew is the kind of dish a cook might offer as a house speciality; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Suppress article making little sense

parts.note: to gag someone is to suppress what they say
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor silences a piece because it is incoherent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gaga is senile or confused, so talking with little sense.

clue.text: PA, say, freshly appointed, learned about residing in US city

parts.note: someone freshly appointed is new to the post
sage means wise or learned

indicators.note: the letter for about lives inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is New York
C, from circa, means about

explanation.surface: A personal assistant, newly hired and well educated, lives in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is not a personal assistant but the Press Association, Britain's national wire service supplying stories to newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Press Association is an example of an organisation that gathers and sells reports to the media.

clue.text: Agreement in Berlin about a very rich sort of coffee

parts.note: ja is German for yes

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the two letters that follow are read backwards

explanation.surface: A German deal over a lavish blend of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A and V round to give VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grown on the Indonesian island is so widely known that the island's name became slang for the drink.

clue.text: Helping to keep Bishop standing

indicators.note: the helping word holds, or keeps, another letter inside it

parts.note: aiding means helping
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Assistance keeps a bishop on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something long-lasting or enduring, as in a standing or lasting arrangement.

clue.text: English occupying street and road during two mornings in European city

indicators.note: the street and road come during, so inside, the pair of mornings
two tells us to take the abbreviation twice

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning

indicators.note: English sits inside, occupying, street and road

explanation.surface: An Englishman takes to the streets over a couple of mornings abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital is a city in Europe, so an example of the category.

clue.text: A source of uplift, making Satan President, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Electing the Devil as head of state might lift the gloom, somebody suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that treats depression lifts a patient's mood, which is uplift in the emotional sense.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's era? Generation with wits running wild is about right

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round, about, the letter for right
running wild means out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A jazz-age writer's period: a clever generation run amok, with all its rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generation' looks like part of the definition beside 'era', but it is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelist F. Scott Fitzgerald chronicled the 1920s jazz age, the decade's popular nickname.

clue.text: Run, missing first place? Nothing magical about me

indicators.note: the letter in first place is missing, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them

explanation.surface: A runner fails to come first and admits to having no special powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is the smuggling sense, as in running guns.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Harry Potter books a person with no magical ability is called by this term, so it fits the self-description.

clue.text: Sea horse? I'm behind it being captured

indicators.note: the later words are captured inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: I'm comes behind, after, it

parts.note: I'm with the apostrophe dropped gives these letters

explanation.surface: A seahorse is out of sight and the speaker follows it into captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, sea and its formal equivalent both mean connected with the ocean, as in sea law.

clue.text: Ugly boil about to appear in face — very unpleasant

indicators.note: the next letters show up inside the face

parts.note: dial is slang for a person's face

indicators.note: ugly suggests a misshapen version, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A nasty spot is about to break out on someone's face.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or appalling is described informally as devilishly bad.

clue.text: Policeman at fault, taking time to wipe out fine

indicators.note: the word takes in a new letter
the new letter removes, wipes out, the one for fine

parts.note: defective means faulty
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A careless officer takes time to clear a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... to wipe out' swaps one letter: T replaces the F of DEFECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain-clothes investigator is a kind of police officer.

clue.text: Mania for cartooning as a form of weapon

indicators.note: a mania for something is that thing followed by the craze word

parts.note: doodling is idle sketching, like cartooning
a bug is a craze or obsession

explanation.surface: Someone's obsession with drawing cartoons becomes a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The cryptic reading is 'a craze for sketching'. The definition is the V-1 flying bomb fired at Britain in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname was given to the German V-1 flying bomb, a weapon.

clue.text: Quietly moved goalposts, initially between editions

indicators.note: the next letter goes between the two edition abbreviations

parts.note: ED is short for edition, so two editions give it twice

indicators.note: only the first letter of goalposts is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone shifted the goalposts discreetly between issues of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge is to move slowly and cautiously, so a stealthy, quiet movement.

clue.text: Ferdinand, say, appearing among working stars

indicators.note: the footballer appears inside the working word

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on
Rio Ferdinand is a former England football captain

explanation.surface: A footballer turns up among the working celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' looks like celebrities to go with the footballer; it is the definition, a constellation. RIO Ferdinand is a famous English footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunter constellation is a group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Request reduced openings for research officers using test-tubes

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the request loses its final letter

parts.note: an invite is a request to come

indicators.note: the openings are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An application for funding is cut back on behalf of laboratory staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in glass', the phrase describes experiments done in laboratory vessels rather than living bodies.

clue.text: Contrived phrase to support Reagan, say, the writer's recalled

parts.note: to back is to support
Ronald Reagan, the US President, was known as Ron

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, so the writer's is my

explanation.surface: A supporter of Reagan remembers a slogan they once wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: A word made by fitting a phrase to an existing name, such as a forced acronym, is a contrived phrase.

clue.text: Daughter engaged in relaxation in new North London location

indicators.note: the inner letters sit inside the two outer ones
daughter is engaged, held, inside relaxation

parts.note: ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: A daughter takes it easy in a new home in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North' does double duty in the surface but only its letter is used; the definition is 'London location'. NEASDEN is a London suburb famed in the satirical magazine Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The suburb is a district of north-west London, a place in the capital.

clue.text: Attractive duck board with front scrubbed

parts.note: duck in cricket and love in tennis both mean a score of zero

indicators.note: the first letter is scrubbed away

parts.note: a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A charming duck is placed on a board that has had its face cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of nought in cricket; love is nought in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endearing and easy to be fond of is appealing or attractive.

clue.text: Literary lion beginning to talk in oblique manner

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books

indicators.note: the beginning letter of talk is taken

explanation.surface: A storybook lion starts speaking, but evasively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary lion' sounds like a celebrated author, but it is the Narnia lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanting or at an angle describes something positioned obliquely.

clue.text: Historic garment seen around origin of native island state

indicators.note: the garment is seen wrapped round another letter

parts.note: a toga was the robe of ancient Rome

indicators.note: the origin is the first letter of native

explanation.surface: An ancient robe worn by a native of an island nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific kingdom is a nation made up of islands.

clue.text: Endless luxury is a bonus

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: plush means luxurious; as a noun it is a rich fabric

explanation.surface: Unlimited luxury is a welcome extra.
explanation.definitionFit: An advantage or extra benefit is called a plus, synonymous with a bonus.

clue.text: Though unkempt, not a bad clearing where specialist plants grow

indicators.note: unkempt means untidy, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A messy but decent woodland clearing where unusual plants flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden for scientific collections of plants is where rare and specialist species are grown.

clue.text: Sentimental nonsense applied to female in error

parts.note: goo is gushing sentimentality

explanation.surface: Mawkish talk aimed at a woman by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is an informal word for a blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Tragic ship, Italian, at sea with American on board

indicators.note: the American is aboard, inside the other letters
at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Italian and an American sail aboard a doomed liner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cunard liner torpedoed in 1915 was a famous maritime disaster, a tragic ship.
